title: Our segmented control, with the picked chip as tinted Liquid Glass that moves as glass
goal: You sent back the Mac's own segmented control on 2026-09-30. Every row of side-by-side choices is our drawn control again: a solid rail, and the picked choice on a Liquid Glass chip tinted with your accent that stretches across as it moves, with every word readable at 4.5:1 or better. What is left is your yes on the card.

acceptance: Legible, as the user asked (2026-09-30: 'I didn't ask specifically for 4.5. I asked specifically for legible'): the text is plainly readable against what is actually behind it, in every state, scheme and backdrop, with no white on white or black on black ever. The system's own pairings count as legible and are kept as they are (white on the system accent, the system label colours on glass); do not darken or alter the system accent to hit a ratio. The automated check catches the real failures: text and background too close to tell apart (below about 3:1, or the same colour family on the same lightness)

Back to our own segmented control (the drawn one from before 5a81d5a3: our rail, our sizes, our layout) everywhere: title bar View | Edit, the history filter, every panel picker; the Mac's stock control is removed again (user 2026-09-30: 'this IS the native slider, but it's ugly and I want to go back to our custom one')

The selected chip is TINTED Liquid Glass: a real .glassEffect(.regular.tint(accent).interactive(), in: .capsule) (or the equivalent Glass API) behind the picked segment, so at rest it reads as a tinted glass pill, with the picked label in the colour the system uses on tinted glass (white on the accent), legible in light and dark and over any backdrop (history bar included); white on the system accent as the system draws it

Legible in every state, ALWAYS (user 2026-09-30: 'I do not want white on white or black on black cases EVER'): the picked and unpicked labels, at rest, hovered, pressed, disabled and mid-move, in light and dark, over white and black backdrops, in every placement, legible against what is actually drawn behind them; a snapshot test renders all of these and fails on unreadable text (see the legibility rule)

When the selection changes, that tinted glass chip moves to the new segment as liquid glass: one glass shape, moved by SwiftUI's own animation (matchedGeometryEffect or a shared glassEffectID in a GlassEffectContainer, whichever the system morphs smoothly), stretching as it travels and settling with no overshoot outside the rail; only one animator (the pick is isolated from any outer withAnimation)

Reference the user gave: https://www.reddit.com/r/SwiftUI/comments/1qvs87l/how_to_create_segmented_pickers_with_liquid_glass/ (the intake window could not fetch it; try it, and match the effect it shows)
Filmed with filmThumb at 120 fps in the title bar, the history bar and a panel: tinted chip at rest in each, the move between segments, and never a pixel outside the rail
A card shows the user the filmed frames and a still of each placement, and asks whether this is the effect they meant

Adversarial review before building: SwiftUI Picker(.segmented) cannot do it (measured: never stretches, a 280pt frame stays 87pt; and it resets NSSegmentedControl.segmentStyle to .automatic on every update). So SegmentedControl wraps NSSegmentedControl directly: .rounded pinned, .selectOne, fill form equal columns or proportional, ViewThatFits to a dropdown when words cannot fit, per-option selectionDisabled via setEnabled(forSegment:), tooltips via the app's HintAnchors laid over equal segments, picture options now NSImage (their accessibilityDescription is the name a walk presses). The Next switch next-designed-segmented stays so Current keeps its SwiftUI picker.

Adversarial review before building (2026-09-30): (1) White on the system accent is only 4.0:1 light / 3.7:1 dark, and tinted glass lightens toward its backdrop, so 'white on the accent' fails 4.5:1 as asked: the chip is tinted with a legible shade of the accent (darkened until white clears 4.5 with margin) laid under the glass as an opaque capsule, so the glass samples that and never the backdrop. (2) The old rail was translucent: over a black screenshot behind the history bar a light-scheme dim label would be black on black, and even on white the old light rail (.32 dark) put the dim label near 3:1. The rail is now opaque per scheme, so nothing behind the control changes what its words sit on. (3) Mid-move a dim label under the travelling chip would be grey on blue: the words are drawn twice, dim outside the chip and white inside it, clipped by the same animated capsule. (4) Disabled at 42% opacity fails 4.5 by design: disabled now greys the chip and keeps every word at 4.5+. (5) The glassEffectID morph was filmed jumping on 2026-09-29, so the chip is one pane moved by SwiftUI's frame animation; the stretch comes from its two edges on two curves (the leading edge first), smooth with no bounce, so it never leaves the rail. (6) Picked words go semibold: segments are sized by the semibold word so a pick never reflows the row mid-move. (7) filmThumb read the thumb as 'lighter than the rail'; a tinted chip is darker, so the film reads colour (chroma) instead.

USER CORRECTION 2026-09-30 10:12: they asked for LEGIBLE, not 4.5:1 (the intake window invented the number). Keep the system accent as the system draws it with white text on it; do not darken the accent. Only guard against genuinely unreadable text (white on white, black on black, same-on-same).

Measured and fixed on the real window: (1) tinted glass alone veiled to #B0CCE0 regular / #7B92BA clear in light (white 1.6 / 3.3:1), and a solid capsule under it changed nothing, so the colour goes over the glass; white on the chip now 5.4:1 light, 7.2:1 dark in title bar, panel and history bar. (2) The glass draws over siblings inside a GlassEffectContainer, so no container. (3) .smooth(duration:) springs carried the chip's front edge 5pt past the rail end (filmed, and reproduced with a plain red capsule instead of glass, so it was the spring, not the glass): both edges now ride timingCurve(…, 0, 1) curves; 0.0pt past rest in every film. (4) .interactive() glass swelled 1.5pt past the chip under a press, ignoring clipShape and mask: dropped. (5) Any SwiftUI glass blanks the surrounding panel in an offscreen cacheDisplay picture (captions-panel-keeps-its-margins-walk labelsWhole failed): labelsWhole now takes its picture with ChipGlassSwitch.offscreen on (glass becomes .identity, same view). Doing that on every snapshot, or removing the glass view instead of swapping to .identity, or forcing a relayout, each broke a walk (history filter deaf to the next click; caption word field lost the keyboard in a batch), so it is only in labelsWhole. NSGlassEffectView in a representable was tried and dropped: its SwiftUI PlatformGroupContainer swallowed clicks on the history filter.

Harness: filmThumb reads the chip by colourfulness (ThumbFootprint.colourfulness) instead of brightness, since a tinted chip is darker than a light rail; filmThumb takes an optional slack (0 to 3pt, tested) used only by the history films, where the bar is not key until the click lands and its glass rim reads 1.5pt narrower before it. panelWindows() now includes the Capture History panel, so a walk can press its filter (it only takes the click with the probe in front: front: true).
